title: Longitudinal monitoring of regional ventilation distribution and ventilator-associated lung injury in pediatric ARDS (MoVe LupARDS study)
summary: As part of the MoVe LeopARD study, we want to investigate whether ventilation-associated lung damage in the context of acute respiratory failure in newborns and children (neonatal/ pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome - nARDS/ pARDS) can be improved with an impact on duration of mechanical ventilation as well as short- to medium-term outcome and mortality.  We are trying to achieve this through individualized ventilation monitoring during long-term mechanical ventilation using electrical impedance tomography (EIT) as well as procedures such as lung ultrasound and biomarker analyses from blood or lung fluid. Over a period of 4 years, at least 120 patients with nARDS/ pARDS (60 intervention group, 60 control group) will be included and monitored and analyzed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Infants/children with mild to severe respiratory failure (nARDS/ pARDS: exogenous, endogenous, infection-associated) and need for intubation with mechanical ventilation according to Montreaux and PALICC-2 guidelines (Emeriaud et al. 2023b; Luca et al. 2017)
- Consent of the parents to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients with palliative care
- Lack of parental consent
- Contraindication against performing an EIT measurement in accordance with the approval (e.g. pacemaker)
